action: library(OrgMassSpecR); args(Digest) to see the digest function
note: loads. Signature: Digest(sequence, enzyme='trypsin', missed=0, IAA=TRUE, N15=FALSE, custom). Defaults are trypsin, 0 missed cleavages, carbamidomethyl-Cys ON by default (IAA=TRUE).

action: Read ?Digest help (Rd2txt) for the trypsin rule and any min-length option
note: Good help. trypsin = cleave C-terminal of K/R EXCEPT when followed by P; trypsin.strict = cleave after every K/R. KP/RP not counted as missed cleavages. NO minimum-length parameter exists; Digest returns every fragment including single residues.

action: Check built-in example.sequence (used in the help examples as HSA)
note: It IS human serum albumin but 585 aa and starts DAHK... = the MATURE chain, not the 609-aa canonical accession. Docs never say which form or give the P02768 accession, so I couldn't trust it for the task. Had to go verify against UniProt.

action: download.file P02768.fasta from rest.uniprot.org to get the real accession sequence
note: Canonical P02768 = 609 aa. Has signal peptide (1-18 MKWVTFISLLFLFSSAYS) + propeptide (19-24 RGVFRR); mature circulating chain is 25-609 = 585 aa, which matches the package's example.sequence. So the tool ships HSA but as the processed form and unlabeled.

action: Digest(seq609, 'trypsin', missed=0/1/2) and Digest(mature585, missed=0); count rows and length distribution
note: Canonical 609 missed=0 => 83 peptides (lengths 1..27), missed=2 => 246. Mature 585 missed=0 => 79. Length filter matters enormously: of the 83, only 42 are >=6 aa and 37 are >=7 aa. Digest itself does no length cutoff.

action: Fetch P02768.json from UniProt and tabulate feature types (PTMs are not in OrgMassSpecR)
note: OrgMassSpecR has no annotation store; modifications must come from UniProt. Feature counts: Modified residue 14, Glycosylation 24, Disulfide bond 17, plus binding/variant/structure features that are not PTMs.

action: Print descriptions of the 14 Modified residue and 24 Glycosylation features to judge search-usability
note: Modified residue = 9 phospho (pS/pT), 4 N6-succinyllysine, 1 N6-methyllysine(alternate) - all defined chemistry. Glycosylation = 22 'N-linked (Glc) glycation lysine' (mostly 'in vitro', non-enzymatic Amadori +hexose) + 2 'N-linked GlcNAc asparagine' that are ONLY in disease variants Redhill/Casebrook (not canonical).

action: Judge whether UniProt mods are directly usable as search mass deltas
note: UniProt gives the site + a NAME ('Phosphoserine') but NO machine-readable mass delta. To use any of these in a mass search I must map each name to a delta myself (phospho +79.966, succinyl +100.016, methyl +14.016, glycation +162.053). The tool does not do this mapping.

action: Read ?FragmentPeptide and args() to see if ETD ions are even supported
note: fragments='by' (CID, b/y) or fragments='cz' (ETD, c/z). Help explicitly maps cz to electron transfer dissociation. So the tool answers Q3 directly.

action: FragmentPeptide('LVNEVTEFAK', fragments='cz') on a real HSA tryptic peptide
note: Returns c-ion and z-ion series ([c1]1+, [c2]1+ ... and z ions). Confirms ETD => c and z. Note: tool labels them 'z'; in ETD the true product is the z-radical (z-dot, z+1.008); a biologist should check whether the tool's z is z or z-dot before matching.
